description: خريجة ثانوي شغوفة بالتقنية والابتكار الصحي. أملك مهارات متقدمة في البرمجة وعلوم الحاسب، وعملت على تطوير ومبرمجة نموذج لجهاز يراقب ويساعد في التعامل مع الحالات الصحية لرواد الفضاء (كالتعامل مع الجروح والسموم). أرغب  بمشاركة  شغفي ومهاراتي البرمجية، والمساهمة في بناء حلول تقنية واعدة تخدم مجال الفضاء والتقنية الصحية
summary:
On long space missions, a small wound can become serious, and rapid evacuation is not possible beyond low Earth orbit. An astronaut has no laboratory and often no doctor, and cannot see bacteria by eye. Healing Pen is a handheld pen that helps an astronaut assess their own wound and guides the next treatment step. It reads wound size, depth, temperature, pH, moisture and a fluorescence index, and places them beside the astronaut's vital signs. A transparent rule-based score rates the risk as Low, Medium or Critical and explains each point. Lower-risk cases receive a care plan and a red-light therapy demonstration. Critical cases send an urgent alert to a ground team through a web dashboard that stores and forwards messages when the link is lost.

The project grew out of our earlier Smart Healing Pen concept, which centered on a nano-silica hydrogel and an antidote. We kept that as a future module and built an electronics prototype and a dashboard, checked with test materials and simulated scenarios. The pen gives early warning signs of possible infection. It does not diagnose or confirm bacteria, and it does not heal wounds. Vital signs and the link to Earth are simulated, and the risk thresholds are not clinically validated. The design draws on NASA research and NASA skin data from spaceflown mice. Future work includes a camera with an optical filter, real vital-sign sensors, an image model trained on clinician-labelled photos, and supervised laboratory testing.
details:
Healing Pen is a handheld pen that helps an astronaut assess their own wound, and the body's response to it, when no doctor is on board.

How it works. The pen reads wound size, depth, temperature, pH, moisture and a fluorescence index, and shows them beside the astronaut's vital signs on a web dashboard. A transparent rule-based score rates the risk as Low, Medium or Critical, and every point has a stated reason. The pen shows the level with a green, yellow or red LED and a buzzer for Critical. Lower-risk cases get a care plan and a red-light therapy demonstration. Critical cases send an urgent alert to a ground team, and the light stays blocked until a flight surgeon decides.

Benefits and impact. An astronaut cannot see bacteria and has no laboratory, so infection can start unnoticed. The pen gives a measured, repeatable early warning of possible infection, and the ground team gets a shared view of the astronaut's condition. If validated, it could help remote clinics and diabetic patients on Earth.

Tools. Arduino-compatible board with C++ firmware, MLX90614 infrared thermometer, VL53L0X distance sensor, pH module, moisture probe, 405 nm LED with light sensor, status LEDs and buzzer. The dashboard is a single page of HTML, CSS and JavaScript that reads the pen over USB with Web Serial.

Creative side. Sensing, risk rating, treatment guidance and a ground alert are combined in one pocket-sized pen. Alerts are stored and forwarded when the link to Earth is lost, and the design is modular, so a hydrogel or antidote can be added later.

Factors we considered. Spaceflight slows wound healing and infection cannot be fully prevented, based on NASA research. We kept the score explainable, and added a time limit, a stop button and physician control over the light. We were also honest about limits. The pen gives warning signs and does not diagnose or detect bacteria. Vital signs and the Earth link are simulated, the thresholds are not clinically validated, and the hydrogel and antidote are future concepts.
